title: Gibson Assembly Protocol
author: N.J. Hillson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6t5heq6

steps.title: Prepare 5X ISO Buffer
steps.instruction: Make 6 ml of 5X ISO Buffer in a 15 ml Falcon tube by mixing the listed reagents and storing the aliquots at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 ml 1 M Tris‑HCl, pH 7.5.
Add 150 µl 2 M MgCl₂.
Add 240 µl 100 mM dNTP mix (25 mM each dGTP, dCTP, dATP, dTTP).
Add 300 µl 1 M DTT.
Add 1.5 g PEG‑8000.
Add 300 µl 100 mM NAD⁺.
Add deionised water to bring the final volume to 6 ml.
Store at –20 °C in 320 ml aliquots.

steps.title: Prepare Gibson Assembly Master Mix
steps.instruction: Combine the components to obtain 1.2 ml of Gibson assembly master mix and keep aliquots at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Add 320 µl 5X ISO Buffer (prepared above).
Add 0.64 µl 10 U ml⁻¹ T5 exonuclease (optimized for 20–150 bp overlaps).
Add 20 µl 2 U ml⁻¹ Phusion polymerase.
Add 160 µl 40 U ml⁻¹ Taq ligase.
Add deionised water to bring the final volume to 1.2 ml.
Store at –20 °C in 15 ml aliquots.

steps.title: Thaw Master Mix Aliquot
steps.instruction: Thaw a 15 ml aliquot of the Gibson assembly master mix and keep it on ice until use.

steps.title: Measure DNA Concentrations
steps.instruction: Determine the concentration (ng ml⁻¹) of each DNA fragment that will be used in the assembly.

steps.title: Set Up Assembly Reaction
steps.instruction: Assemble the reaction to a total volume of 20 ml using the thawed master mix, vector backbone, equimolar inserts, and water.

substeps.instruction: Add linearized vector backbone (100 ng).
Add each additional assembly piece in an amount equimolar to the backbone.
Add 15 ml of the thawed Gibson assembly master mix.
Add deionised water to bring the total volume to 20 ml.

steps.title: Incubate Assembly Reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate the 20 ml assembly mixture at 50 °C for 60 minutes, then place the tube on ice.

steps.title: Transform or Analyze Assembly
steps.instruction: Introduce 5 ml of the assembly reaction into 100 ml of competent E. coli, or run a diagnostic agarose gel to assess assembly success.

substeps.instruction: Transform the reaction into competent cells.
Alternatively, load an aliquot on an agarose gel for diagnostic analysis.
